handoff.outcome: Audited duration/duration.js against the spec: parses h/m/s duration strings into milliseconds, units in any order, each at most once, throws TypeError on anything invalid. Implementation confirmed correct.
handoff.deliverables: Read duration/duration.js and duration/duration.test.js. Ran `node --test` in duration/ — all 3 existing tests pass. Additionally manually exercised edge cases not covered by the test file: decimals ("1.5h"), negative numbers ("-1h"), wrong case ("1H"), leading/trailing whitespace (" 1h", "1h "), trailing garbage after a valid unit ("1h2"), unit with no number ("s"), unordered combos ("1s2h3m"), and zero values ("0h0m0s") — all behaved correctly (valid inputs parsed, invalid inputs threw TypeError).
handoff.decision_refs: No repairs needed; no decompose or escalate used — audit found the implementation conforms to the described behavior.
handoff.resume_context: No follow-up work required. If further hardening is ever desired, the only theoretical non-spec gap noted was large numeric inputs (e.g. absurdly long digit strings) relying on plain Number() with no overflow handling — not a violation of the stated spec, so no action taken.
